learning_objective: 🎯 Understand that development means different things to different people, and learn how to compare the development of countries using income, health, and education indicators.

key_vocabulary.definition: A process that creates growth, progress, and positive change in the economic, social, and demographic components of a society.
The average income of a country, calculated by dividing the total national income by the total population.
The number of children that die before the age of one year as a proportion of 1,000 live children born in that particular year.
A composite statistic published by UNDP combining life expectancy, education, and per capita income indicators.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Development goals vary. What may be development for one person may be destructive for another. For example, building a dam means development for an industrialist (more electricity), but it means destruction for a tribal person whose land gets submerged.

People want more income, but they also seek non-material goals like equal treatment, freedom, security, and respect. A safe working environment or job security is often preferred over a high-paying but highly stressful and unsafe job.

The World Bank compares countries solely based on Per Capita Income (Rich, Middle, Low-income countries). However, this hides disparities. The UNDP compares countries based on the educational levels of the people, their health status, and per capita income (HDI).

Development should not compromise the needs of future generations. Groundwater depletion and environmental degradation (like climate change) are prime examples of unsustainable development. We have not inherited the world from our forefathers; we have borrowed it from our children.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ The Average Illusion
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine Country A has 5 citizens earning: ₹9500, ₹10500, ₹9800, ₹10000, ₹10200. Average = ₹10000. Country B has 5 citizens earning: ₹500, ₹500, ₹500, ₹500, ₹48000. Average = ₹10000! Both have the same average income, but Country B has extreme inequality. This is why Per Capita Income hides the real picture!

exam_tips: 📌 Differentiate clearly between the World Bank's criterion (only Per Capita Income) and the UNDP's criteria (Health, Education, and Income). This is a guaranteed board question.
📌 Kerala has a lower Per Capita Income than Maharashtra/Haryana but a much better HDI due to its excellent health and educational infrastructure (low IMR, high literacy).
📌 Remember the definitions of IMR, Literacy Rate, and Net Attendance Ratio word-for-word.
quick_recap: ⭐ National development refers to the ability of a country to improve the social welfare of its people.
⭐ Money in your pocket cannot buy all the goods and services you need to live well (e.g., a pollution-free environment, protection from infectious diseases).
⭐ Sustainable development requires using renewable resources and halting the over-extraction of non-renewable resources like crude oil.
